Suppose $X$ is a continuous random variable with support $S = [0, 100]$. We wish to carry out a hypothesis test with the following null and alternative hypotheses:

- $H_{0}:X∼U[0, 100]$
- $H_{1}:X≁U[0, 100]$

A random sample is carried out, and the sample data is shown below. Calculate the expected frequency $E_{i}$ for each class of observations.

| Class | $0 \le x_{i} < 20$ | $20 \le x_{i} < 40$ | $40 \le x_{i} < 70$ | $70 \le x_{i} \le 100$ |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Observed Frequency $(O_{i})$ | $32$ | $28$ | $48$ | $42$ |
| Expected Frequency $(E_{i})$ | {{field-1}} | {{field-2}} | {{field-3}} | {{field-4}} |

A forestry researcher categorizes trees in a particular forest depending on their height. Tree heights range from $5$ to $20$ meters. The researcher wishes to carry out a hypothesis test with the following null and alternative hypotheses:

- $H_{0}$: The tree heights are distributed uniformly.
- $H_{1}$: The tree heights are not distributed uniformly.

A random sample of trees in the forest is taken, and the frequency distribution of tree heights is shown below. Calculate the expected frequency $E_{i}$ for each height category.

| Height ($m$) | $5 \le x_{i} < 10$ | $10 \le x_{i} < 12$ | $12 \le x_{i} < 16$ | $16 \le x_{i} \le 20$ |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Observed Frequency $(O_{i})$ | $40$ | $20$ | $28$ | $32$ |
| Expected Frequency $(E_{i})$ | {{field-1}} | {{field-2}} | {{field-3}} | {{field-4}} |
